meta.title: The Little Prince Simulator
meta.notes: All dialogue is original writing inspired by Antoine de Saint-Exupery's The Little Prince. 'heart' goes up when the player chooses curiosity and care; max is 8.

busy_grownups.title: Busy Grown-Ups
busy_grownups.text: Grown-ups can get so busy with 'serious' things that they stop noticing what really matters.

responsibility.title: The Rose
responsibility.text: Loving something means being responsible for it, even when it is hard to understand.

authority.title: The King
authority.text: Real authority rests on reason. Power over nothing is not power at all.

owning_vs_caring.title: The Businessman
owning_vs_caring.text: Owning something is not the same as caring for it. We matter to the things we look after.

invisible.title: The Goose's Secret
invisible.text: The most important things can't be seen with the eyes, only felt with the heart. Time spent together is what makes someone unique to you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Davis Hall, University at Buffalo. 3:07 A.M.

lines.speaker: student
lines.text: Forty-two errors. Why are there forty-two errors?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Outside the window, the sky over campus is full of stars. You haven't looked up once tonight.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Excuse me... will you code me a sheep?

choices.text: Keep typing. "Not now. I'm busy with something important."

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Important? More important than a sheep?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You sigh and finally turn around. A small boy with golden hair and a long scarf is standing there, very serious.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small boy with golden hair and a long scarf is standing there, very serious.

lines.speaker: student
lines.text: Fine. class Box: pass. Your sheep is inside the box.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Oh! That is exactly the one I wanted.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: From very far away. From a planet hardly bigger than a house.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Would you like to hear about it? Grown-ups never want to. They're always busy with serious matters.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: This is home. Asteroid B-612.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Every morning I take care of it: I water my flower, I sweep out my volcanoes, and I pull up the baobab sprouts before they grow too big.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: I'm not saying I'm thirsty (or maybe I am).

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Want to do the honors?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You water the rose.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: Fine. That's... acceptable.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: Wonderful. I'll just wilt quietly, then.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She does not wilt quietly.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: There's a draft. I can't bear drafts. Bring me my glass cover, please. And do something about the tigers.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: There are no tigers on my planet. And tigers don't eat flowers.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: (to you) She says such strange things. I love her, but I don't understand her at all.

choices.text: "Maybe try to understand her before you decide anything."
"She's impossible. You should go see the universe."

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: I think... her four thorns are all she has to protect herself. Maybe her pride is a kind of thorn too.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: But I still need to see the universe. I need to understand things. Then I'll know how to love her properly.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: Go, then. I was proud and foolish, and I'm sorry. I love you. I always have.

lines.speaker: rose
lines.text: So you're leaving.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Goodbye.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Much later, he would wonder whether he had judged her by her words instead of by what she did for him: she had filled his whole planet with her scent.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: I left on a morning when the wild birds were migrating. I held onto them and flew out into the stars.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: The first planet I reached belonged to a king.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Ah! Here is a subject! Approach, so that I can see you better.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: There is nowhere to stand except on the robe. The prince stays where he is. He is very tired from the journey, and he yawns.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Yawning? Before your king? That is simply not done! Stop at once!

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Then... I order you to yawn! Yawning is a curiosity to me. Go on! It is an order!

choices.text: "Why order something I was already doing?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The prince tries to yawn. Now that he's been ordered to, he can't.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Hm. Then I order you to sometimes yawn and sometimes... not yawn. Yes. That is my command.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: If I commanded my royal cook to bake a cake in one second, and he failed, whose fault would that be? His, or mine?

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Yours, I think.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Exactly. A king must only ask what can actually be done.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Excellent! What a well-mannered subject. It has been so long since I had one.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Then could you order the sun to set? I love sunsets.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Let me consult my almanac... This evening, at about seven-forty. You'll see how well I am obeyed.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: (to you) So he can only order things that were going to happen anyway.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Don't go! I'll make you a minister. Minister of Justice!

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: But there's no one here to judge.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Then you'll judge yourself. That is the hardest of all. If you can judge yourself well, you are truly wise.

choices.text: Accept the title of Minister of Justice.
"I can judge myself anywhere. I'll keep traveling."

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The prince sits and waits. No one comes to be judged. There is an old rat somewhere on the planet, but it has nothing to say.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: A title over nothing is still nothing. I'm leaving after all.

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: Then... I make you my ambassador!

lines.speaker: king
lines.text: I... I make you my ambassador!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He says it with a great air of authority, as if leaving had been his idea all along.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Grown-ups are very strange.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: The next planet belonged to a man who was too busy to look up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in a suit sits at a desk covered in papers, scribbling numbers. He doesn't raise his head.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Busy. Very busy. I'm a serious man. I don't have time for chatter.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: What are you counting?

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Those tiny sparkly dots up there. The ones dreamers waste their evenings staring at.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Yes, yes, the stars. Five hundred and one million of them, and they're all mine.

choices.text: "That's a lot. Want some help counting?"

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Finally, someone sensible! Here. Count these. Every star you count goes in the ledger.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Do with them? Nothing. I own them.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: It makes me rich. And being rich lets me buy more stars, if anyone discovers new ones.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Enough questions. Make yourself useful and count.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Click the stars to count them. The ledger is waiting.

minigame.description: Each click adds stars to a counter that climbs pointlessly. A 'Stop and look' button appears after a few clicks. Report 'looked' if the player presses it, or 'kept_counting' if the timer runs out first.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You stop clicking. The counter freezes. For a moment, you just look at the sky.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stars aren't numbers at all. They shimmer. Some of them seem to be laughing.

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: What are you doing? You've lost count! Now I'll have to start the whole column over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The counter climbs higher and higher. Your finger aches. The number means nothing at all.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: You counted so many. Did you see a single one?

lines.speaker: businessman
lines.text: Tell you what. For your trouble, I'll sign a thousand stars over to you. I'll write it on a slip of paper and lock it in a drawer.

choices.text: "No, thank you. What would I even do with them?"

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The businessman writes 1,000 on a slip of paper, locks it in his drawer, and goes straight back to counting.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: (to you) My stars are in a drawer. I can't even see them from here.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Back home I have a flower. I give her water every morning. I have three volcanoes too, and I keep them clean.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Because I take care of them, they're better off. Your stars don't even know you exist.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The businessman opens his mouth, finds nothing to say, and goes back to his numbers.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Looking at all those stars, I kept thinking about one of them. Mine. And the flower on it.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: After that, my journey brought me all the way to Earth. And to you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Davis Hall. The windows are turning pale blue. Dawn is almost here.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: That's my story. And now I have to go home. My flower is all alone, and she only has four thorns.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: On my way to you, I met a goose. A big gray one, right outside this building.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: She hissed at me too, at first. Then she asked me to tame her.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: It's when you spend so much time with someone that they become different from everyone else. They become yours, and you become theirs.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: She told me a secret: the things that matter most can't be seen with your eyes. You see them with your heart.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: She also told me why geese fly in a V. Each one makes the wind a little easier for the one behind. Nobody crosses the sky alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your laptop buzzes. Messages from your team: 'got coffee', 'where r u??', 'we fixed the bug i think lol'.

lines.speaker: student
lines.text: My team. We came here to build something together.

choices.text: Open the laptop. There's still work to do.
Close the laptop and go find your team.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You turn back to the screen. When you look up again, the boy is gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Only a small text file is left open on your desktop: sheep_in_a_box.py.

lines.speaker: prince
lines.text: Good. They're your flock, I think. And your rose.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You turn toward the door. When you look back, the boy is gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Only a small text file is left open on your desktop: sheep_in_a_box.py.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ending: The Tamed.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sun comes up over campus. You still have bugs to fix, but somehow it doesn't feel so heavy.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tonight, when you look up, one of those stars will be laughing. You'll know which one.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ending: The Grown-Up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You finish the code just as the sun rises. Zero errors. It should feel like more than it does.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Somewhere far away, a small boy is watering a flower. Maybe, if you listen more closely next time, you'll understand why that matters.
